title: podman build in 6.0.x no longer honors `env` and `http_proxy` in `containers.conf`
body:
### Issue Description

After upgrading Podman from `5.8.3` to `6.0.x`, `podman build` no longer honors the `http_proxy = false` directive and custom `env` settings configured in `containers.conf`. Instead, it always inherits host shell proxy environment variables (e.g. `http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1080`) unless the opposite option (`--http-proxy=false`) is explicitly passed on the CLI.

#### Setup & Context
I have a proxy service running on my local host machine, and in my shell environment I have:
```bash
export http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1080
```

Because I can't pass `127.0.0.1` to a container as a proxy environment variable (since `127.0.0.1` inside a container refers to the container's loopback interface where no proxy is running), I work around this by having the following `containers.conf` configuration:
```toml
[containers]
http_proxy = false
env = [
  "http_proxy=http://host.containers.internal:1080"
]
```

Before 6.0.x, the behavior between `podman run` and `podman build` was consistent with this `containers.conf` configuration. However, this is no longer the case in 6.0.x—`podman build` ignores `containers.conf`, causing build steps to inherit `127.0.0.1:1080` from the host shell and fail with connection refused errors.


### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Set up host shell proxy environment variable:
   ```bash
   export http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1080
   ```

2. Configure `~/.config/containers/containers.conf`:
   ```toml
   [containers]
   http_proxy = false
   env = [
     "http_proxy=http://host.containers.internal:1080"
   ]
   ```

3. Compare `podman run` vs `podman build`:
   ```bash
   # Test podman run:
   podman run --rm alpine env | grep -i proxy

   # Test podman build:
   podman build --no-cache -f - . << 'EOF'
   FROM alpine
   RUN env | grep -i proxy
   EOF
   ```


### Describe the results you received

`podman run --rm alpine env | grep -i proxy` correctly prints:
```
http_proxy=http://host.containers.internal:1080
```

Whereas `podman build` prints:
```
http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1080
```

`podman run` honors `containers.conf` (`http_proxy = false` and `env = [...]`), properly setting `http://host.containers.internal:1080`.
In contrast, `podman build` ignores `containers.conf` and inherits `127.0.0.1:1080` directly from the host shell, causing network requests during build `RUN` steps (e.g. `RUN apk update`) to fail with connection refused errors against `127.0.0.1:1080`.


### Describe the results you expected

With `http_proxy = false` and custom proxy `env` configured in `containers.conf`, `podman build` should honor `http_proxy = false` to disable host `127.0.0.1` proxy passthrough, while applying `[containers] env` settings (`http_proxy=http://host.containers.internal:1080`) transiently during build `RUN` steps without leaking proxy environment variables into committed image metadata (`ENV` directives) (which was the behavior in 5.8.x and consistent with `podman run`).

comments.body: A friendly reminder that this issue had no activity for 30 days.

This is still valid. I'm still suffering from having to manually change many build scripts to add `--build-arg` in order to make them work.

Simply configuring ambient environment variables like `http_proxy=http://host.containers.internal:1080 podman build` won't work as podman will otherwise unable to pull images from the internet as the proxy is only valid when inside of the container.

I hope the fix to this regression could get merged so users can at least have a way to configure ambient proxies instead of having to dig through and change build scripts which the authors often doesn't consider the case where the internet is only behind a proxy.
